messages.subject: First timer for unmarked
parts:
Dear all,

This is my first time using unmarked with function pcount for N-Mixture Models.
I have data for 29 ungulate species for 13 sites which was counter either 2 times or 3 times.
I am consulting a book (Kery and Royle 2015) and that's how I tried using a dummy data to see what happens.

Like all software and codes, I was provided with a result. I would appreciate if somebody could help me interpret it.

Inference for Bugs model at "model1.txt", fit using jags,
 3 chains, each with 25000 iterations (first 5000 discarded), n.thin = 20
 n.sims = 3000 iterations saved
         mu.vect sd.vect   2.5%    25%    50%    75%   97.5%  Rhat n.eff
lambda     5.926   7.838  1.721  2.615  3.582  5.828  25.808 1.010   570
p          0.313   0.153  0.044  0.192  0.314  0.428   0.602 1.011   510
deviance  90.742   7.231 77.008 85.499 90.929 96.154 104.136 1.001  2200

For each parameter, n.eff is a crude measure of effective sample size,
and Rhat is the potential scale reduction factor (at convergence, Rhat=1).

DIC info (using the rule, pD = var(deviance)/2)
pD = 26.1 and DIC = 116.9
DIC is an estimate of expected predictive error (lower deviance is better).

How do I explain this in my results.

All the help is appreciated.

regards,
Zaara

messages.subject: AW: [unmarked] First timer for unmarked
parts:
Dear Zaara,

 

to be honest, I think I would really read up on the binomial N-mixture model, e g., by reading a couple of times the beginning of Chapter 6 in that Kéry & Royle (2016) book that you mention, until you get a grasp of “what happens” and what the model (and therefore, these parameters) mean. That’s all in there and I don’t think it’s efficient if somebody takes the time now to explain all that to you right now.

 

Side-comment: you use JAGS, not unmarked, so your question is more appropriate for the HMecology sister list.

 

Best regards  --- Marc
